label: Write the note
hint: The agent writes or updates the ticket note from the request in the field, and asks its open questions separately.

label: Send the answers
hint: Sends your answers to the open questions at once; the agent updates the note.

label: Set the shape
hint: The agent lays down the note's “Forme” section (modules, signatures, contracts) without writing code; the field can refine it.

label: Write the invariants (red), then check the alignment
hint: Writes the invariant tests, red, from the note or from the pseudo-code in the field, then checks the alignment (align.md): on gaps, fixes the tests and checks again, 3 rounds at most; doesn't commit.

label: Read as pseudo-code
hint: Turns each invariant test not yet read into pseudo-code, case by case, with its edge cases and warnings; a file that changed is read again by itself; « Read again » (one file) and « Read all again » redo a reading.

label: Check the alignment
hint: Checks that each “→ invariant” line has a test that truly observes it, that each test has its line, and that the shape matches the files.

label: Prepare the commit
hint: Picks and stages the files of the next commit and proposes its message, shown here before committing.

label: ✓ Commit
hint: Commits with the proposed message, as shown.

label: Generate this module
hint: Implements the chosen module from the note and its shape, with ponytail, and runs the tests; does not commit.

label: Commit this module
hint: Commits the chosen module's changes: one commit following the project's convention, or a fixup if it is already committed.

label: ✓ Approve → commit → next
hint: Commits the reviewed module, then generates the next one.

label: Generate the remaining modules
hint: The agent hands the remaining modules to Opus agents in parallel and reviews each diff; does not commit; long and costly.

label: Commit the modules
hint: Commits each module with uncommitted changes, one commit per module in the shape's order (a fixup for a module already committed).

label: Review the diff
hint: Reviews the chosen diff, or the current changes, with the guide's four questions (§5.1), duplication and file headers.

label: Run the checks and the ponytail review
hint: Runs the project's checks (typecheck, tests, invariants, lint) and shows the result, and the ponytail review at the same time; Run again on one check runs only that one, without the ponytail review.

label: Ponytail review
hint: Started with the checks: reviews the whole branch — over-engineering, duplication, note aligned with the code, edge cases, security, dead code; changes nothing.

label: Apply the review
hint: The agent applies the review remarks it judges right (all of them, or the one of Apply), each as a fixup of the commit concerned, and says which ones it discards.
text: Apply the remarks of {{out}}/ponytail.md that you judge right, each as a fixup of the commit that owns the code (/gear-fix-up if it exists), adding nothing else; say which ones you discard and why. Then write {{out}}/ponytail-applied.json: {"applied":["<file>:L<line>", …]}, the address heading each applied remark, plus those it already holds if it is newer than ponytail.md. Only this one (empty: all of them): {{text}}

label: Fold the fixups
hint: Folds the “fixup!” commits into their targets before opening the PR; does not push.

label: Approve the feature (open the PR)
hint: No PR yet: pushes the branch and opens the PR, title and description following the project's convention.

label: Diagnose the CI
hint: PR open: reads the state of its CI and, on failure, gives the probable cause and the fix; fixes nothing.

label: Release candidate
hint: PR open: publishes a release candidate following the project's procedure and installs it for you, keeping the previous one; long, as it waits for the CI.

label: PR merged → back to the base
hint: PR merged: goes back to the base, updates it and deletes the local branch.

label: Official release
hint: PR merged: publishes the official release following the project's procedure; pre-releases are deleted only with your agreement.

label: Load the PR
hint: Fetches the PR without touching your working copy, to review it.

label: Open in a worktree
hint: Creates a worktree of the PR following the project's convention and sets it up (dependencies…); a "PR #n" robot is added there, after the trust question.

label: Unload
hint: The repository's agent removes the PR's worktree (refused if changes remain); this robot leaves with it.

label: Review the note
hint: Reviews the PR's note: decisions to discuss, gaps, misclassified invariants.

label: Review the commits
hint: Reviews the PR commit by commit: the four questions, duplication, file headers, the story the commits tell.

label: On-screen test plan
hint: Prepares the list of what to try by hand, and how to run the PR.

label: Publish the review
hint: Publishes the review draft on GitHub, as is, with the chosen verdict.

label: Vibe
hint: The agent picks up at the first step not done and chains everything up to the release candidate; a blocking question waits for you without stopping it; the banner stops it; long and costly.

label: Where am I?
hint: Asks the gear-guide skill for the next step, from the state of the repository and the question in the field.

label: Ask without changing
hint: Sends the question in the field, telling the agent not to change anything.
text:
{{text}}

(Answer only: do not modify any file and do not run anything that modifies anything.)

label: 💬 Comment
hint: Quotes the item in the field, to comment on it before sending.

label: ✗ Needs rework
hint: Quotes the case in the field, to say what to change.

label: Feedback → fixup
hint: Prepares in the field a feedback to fix as a fixup of the module concerned.
text: Feedback to fix, as a fixup of the module concerned:

label: Propose the commands
hint: The agent looks for how to start the project (README, package.json, process-compose, Makefile, AGENTS.md, .bashrc aliases…) and proposes its commands; with no project file, the app adopts them; otherwise it adds those whose name is not in it yet, leaving the others untouched. The field can guide it.
